_comment: Filtering rules for the detection pass, loaded at runtime by HelperDenylist::LoadFromFile (src/detection/HelperDenylist.h). Two independent jobs live here. (1) pathFragments/helperBasenames/launcherBasenames reject a PROCESS that would otherwise be mistaken for the game it sits next to - crash handlers, installers, redistributables, anti-cheat services, store launchers (DESIGN.md 1.4 step 3). (2) "exclusions" rejects things that ARE correctly identified but are never what someone is streaming - browsers, wallpaper animators, overlays, voice chat, vendor tooling. See src/detection/IndexExclusions.h for why that needs to be its own concept rather than an entry in aliases.json: the alias table can only rename an entry, never suppress it, so anything installed stays permanently eligible to win a poll. Wallpaper Engine is the case that forced it - it is a real Steam app, so it gets a real game's confidence tier and can beat the actual game on working-set size. If this file is missing or fails to parse, HelperDenylist::BuiltInFallback() supplies the same seed content compiled in, so a corrupted or deleted data file degrades to 'as if this file were untouched', never to 'no filtering at all'. Community PRs against this file are how false-positive reports get fixed without a release; see README.md. All basename and displayName entries may use '*' as a wildcard matching any run of characters, and all matching is case-insensitive.

exclusions._comment: WHAT THIS IS FOR CHANGED. It used to be the only thing standing between a driver package and someone's Twitch category, which is a job a denylist cannot do - a real session produced three false positives in one morning (Opera GX, Wallpaper Engine, Microsoft 365) with 47 more of the same kind already indexed and waiting. Uncurated Uninstall-registry entries are now prompt-only by default (CategoryResolver::isPromptOnly), so nothing here is load-bearing for correctness any more. These entries suppress the QUESTION for things nobody would ever stream, so the prompt stays rare enough to be worth reading. basenames/pathFragments skip a running process before the poll pays for OpenProcess. platformIds/displayNames/installRootFragments keep the entry out of the install index entirely. Prefer platformIds - a Steam appid is stable forever, whereas a displayName carrying a version number is a rule with an expiry date; use a trailing '*' for anything versioned. IMPORTANT: do NOT add creative or dev apps here. Photoshop, Krita, FL Studio, VS Code and friends are deliberately detectable and are mapped to real Twitch categories in aliases.json.
